subtitle: Per-symbol coverage of the C++ <cfloat> header. SHIPPED 2026-08-25. Macro-only, like <climits>, so it contributes no re_std:: names -- its contribution is availability. The gap it fills is the C11 set C++17 adopted: the *_DECIMAL_DIG, *_TRUE_MIN and *_HAS_SUBNORM families, recovered from GCC/Clang builtins where the platform header predates C++17. Where no builtin exists (MSVC) a missing macro stays missing and is #ifdef-testable rather than being filled with an invented value. Two silent traps are documented on their rows: *_MIN is the smallest positive NORMAL value rather than the smallest positive value, and FLT_ROUNDS is not a constant expression. re_std::numeric_limits<T> is the better answer everywhere outside a preprocessor conditional.
legend_blurb: <cfloat> provides the floating-point limit macros (radix, precision, range, rounding) for float, double and long double.

symbols.name: FLT_RADIX
symbols.notes: Base of the exponent representation, 2 on every IEEE-754 target. Macros have no namespace, so there is no re_std:: spelling and none is invented. re_std's contribution is availability: the umbrella guarantees the macro is in scope, and the module fills it in from a compiler builtin where the platform's own header predates it. Every gap-fill is #ifndef-guarded -- a platform that answered is never overridden.

symbols.name: FLT_ROUNDS
symbols.notes: NOT A CONSTANT EXPRESSION -- it reflects the current rounding mode, which fesetround() can change at run time, so unlike every other macro in this header it cannot appear in #if or static_assert.

symbols.name: FLT_EVAL_METHOD
symbols.notes: The width intermediate results are computed at: -1 indeterminable, 0 operand width, 1 double, 2 long double. Worth checking on x87 targets, where 2 is common and float arithmetic quietly carries extra precision. Gap-filled from __FLT_EVAL_METHOD__.

symbols.name: DECIMAL_DIG
symbols.notes: Round-trip digits for the widest supported type. Gap-filled from __DECIMAL_DIG__.

symbols.name: FLT_MANT_DIG / DBL_MANT_DIG / LDBL_MANT_DIG
symbols.notes: Macros have no namespace, so there is no re_std:: spelling and none is invented. re_std's contribution is availability: the umbrella guarantees the macro is in scope, and the module fills it in from a compiler builtin where the platform's own header predates it. Every gap-fill is #ifndef-guarded -- a platform that answered is never overridden.

symbols.name: FLT_DIG / DBL_DIG / LDBL_DIG
symbols.notes: Decimal digits that survive a decimal -> binary -> decimal round trip. Distinct from *_DECIMAL_DIG, which counts the other direction.

symbols.name: FLT_MIN_EXP / MAX_EXP / MIN_10_EXP / MAX_10_EXP (all three types)
symbols.notes: Macros have no namespace, so there is no re_std:: spelling and none is invented. re_std's contribution is availability: the umbrella guarantees the macro is in scope, and the module fills it in from a compiler builtin where the platform's own header predates it. Every gap-fill is #ifndef-guarded -- a platform that answered is never overridden.

symbols.name: FLT_MIN / FLT_MAX / FLT_EPSILON (all three types)
symbols.notes: TRAP: *_MIN is the smallest positive NORMAL value, not the smallest positive value -- *_TRUE_MIN is the latter, and for double the two differ by sixteen orders of magnitude (2.2e-308 against 4.9e-324).

symbols.name: FLT_DECIMAL_DIG / DBL_DECIMAL_DIG / LDBL_DECIMAL_DIG
symbols.notes: Digits needed to round-trip the type through decimal text (9 for float, 17 for double). C++17 adopted this from C11, so libraries older than that provide the C++98 set and stop -- code using it fails to compile even though the compiler knows the value perfectly well. Recovered from the matching GCC/Clang builtin, which is the compiler stating a fact about its own float format. MSVC exposes no such builtins, so on that compiler a missing macro STAYS MISSING and is #ifdef-testable: a wrong value would be far worse than an absent one. RE_STD AHEAD OF STD in reach: available at C++98 tiers on any compiler publishing the builtin.

symbols.name: FLT_TRUE_MIN / DBL_TRUE_MIN / LDBL_TRUE_MIN
symbols.notes: Smallest positive value INCLUDING subnormals. C++17 adopted this from C11, so libraries older than that provide the C++98 set and stop -- code using it fails to compile even though the compiler knows the value perfectly well. Recovered from the matching GCC/Clang builtin, which is the compiler stating a fact about its own float format. MSVC exposes no such builtins, so on that compiler a missing macro STAYS MISSING and is #ifdef-testable: a wrong value would be far worse than an absent one. Substituting *_MIN for this is not a rounding difference -- see the *_MIN entry. RE_STD AHEAD OF STD in reach.

symbols.name: FLT_HAS_SUBNORM / DBL_HAS_SUBNORM / LDBL_HAS_SUBNORM
symbols.notes: TRISTATE, not boolean: -1 indeterminable, 0 absent, 1 present. GCC's __FLT_HAS_DENORM__ is 0/1 only, so the derived macro can never produce -1 -- a narrowing of the answer, not a wrong one, since the compiler does know. C++17 adopted this from C11, so libraries older than that provide the C++98 set and stop -- code using it fails to compile even though the compiler knows the value perfectly well.
